item.content:encoded:
As others have said, I like the idea but to me it just needs 'more'. This could be more creepy and sinister without being pure evil and for me there needs to be greater concequence, maybe through greater personal cost.

If the concept supports it I would like to see some clever form of decay to the blood opals. Without further sacrifice from the individual the jewels could lose their lustre, turn grey, crumble to dust. Something to give this item a small lasting comitment that could quickly become taxing through purchasing more and more blood opals.

Imagine you return to the the manufacturer complaining the item has lost its lustre to be told "oh thats no problem, you just have to 'feed' (please find another term for that) it". Your massive investment (I would assume these are expensive) becomes null and void unless you keep paying its price.

This unknowing entry into a binding contract for me gives it a little more sinister edge. Others may think differently but that would be my idea. +1.

item.content:encoded: Both 009 and 409 are autocatalytic; they turn stuff they touch into more of themselves. This isn't true of 578, which behaves like a normal chemical reaction when brought into contact with blood. 009 is implied to come from another reality, something 578 is definitely not. The point is, there are some superficial similarities, but at the core they are very different.

item.content:encoded:
I have to agree that the concept is solid, but the execution is slightly lackluster. I recommend deleting this before it's officially deleted and polishing it for a little while more.

The thing that got me (positively) was that it sort of reminded me of the idea of blood diamonds. You know, precious gems mined in a war zone and sold to finance the combat, but people keep buying them anyone because it's pretty and sparkling and every kiss begins with kay! This is just a little more literal, and some people might think that's a failing, but I don't think so. Because the true horror of this SCP isn't that there's a liquid that turns blood into crystal, although that's pretty horrifying, it's that people keep buying the crystals anyway. And that's why I think the MCD connection isn't tacked on, but perfectly appropriate.

Upvoted for now, hopefully you can polish out any issues and turn this around, because the concept really deserves it!
